topic: The Fractal Logic of Towers: From Ternary Systems to Sierpinski Triangles
target_audience: University students in Computer Science or Mathematics

outline.topic: The Fractal Logic of Towers: From Ternary Systems to Sierpinski Triangles
outline.target_audience: University students in Computer Science or Mathematics

sections.title: The Ternary Foundation
sections.content: Introduce ternary (base-3) counting as the fundamental language of state. Explain how numbers 0, 1, 2 represent the movement between three pegs in the Towers of Hanoi.
sections.example: Representing the state of 3 disks: '000' (all on peg A) to '222' (all on peg C).

sections.title: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Introduce the constraint: disks can only move to an adjacent peg (cyclic constraint). Connect this physical constraint to the ternary sequence where each move corresponds to adding 1 in Gray-code-like ternary.
sections.example: A mechanical 'Frog' robot hopping disks only between adjacent pegs A↔B and B↔C.

sections.title: The Sierpinski Connection
sections.content: Visualize the state-space of the constrained Towers of Hanoi. As the number of disks increases, the valid paths between states form a geometric Sierpinski Triangle.
sections.example: An animation showing a single triangle connecting three states, then recursively splitting into smaller triangles as the disk count increases.

sections.title: Unified Traversal Logic
sections.content: Demonstrate that the optimal path to solve the constrained Towers of Hanoi is equivalent to tracing the perimeter of a Sierpinski triangle graph.
sections.example: Using a path-finding 'Ant' climbing the edges of a Sierpinski fractal to find the shortest route between the start and end configurations.

storyboard.title: The Ternary Foundation
lecture_lines: Ternary counting represents states of Towers of Hanoi.
Each digit corresponds to one of three pegs.
Movement sequences are defined by ternary transitions.
animations: Create a visual representation of 3^n using a grid of squares. Color: #FFFFFF.
Morph the grid into a nested triangle structure to illustrate growth. Color: #FFD700.
Label the base case n=1 with a distinct marker. Color: #00FF00.

storyboard.title: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Constraint limits movement to adjacent pegs only.
Disks hop between A, B, and C.
This structure forms a cyclic ternary path.
animations: Display a tower with three colored discs on a peg. Color: #FF4500.
Animate the movement of discs following a constraint path. Color: #1E90FF.
Highlight illegal moves with a red flashing warning sign. Color: #FF0000.

storyboard.title: The Sierpinski Connection
lecture_lines: Map constrained state-space to a geometric graph.
Recursive connections build a Sierpinski Triangle.
Higher disk counts increase fractal depth.
animations: Iteratively subdivide the triangle into four smaller triangles. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show the recursive removal of the central triangle. Color: #FF4500.

storyboard.title: Unified Traversal Logic
lecture_lines: Optimal solutions follow the triangle's perimeter.
Path-finding logic mirrors the fractal structure.
Every move maps to a geometric step.
animations: Visualize the state space graph for the constraints. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate a path traversal from start to end node. Color: #1E90FF.
Place a green target icon at the final node. Color: #00FF00.
